hero.headline: Neighbors oppose proposed 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95 in St. Lucie County
hero.body:
A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but not without pushback from neighbors who say it will transform the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

The development would include 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres, an area equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches. Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on property that has been in her family for decades. Lewis said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "I have dogs that have 10 acres to run around. I have horses that have 10 acres to run around. It's gone," Lewis said. "We will be surrounded. I think that there's plenty of other places for them to build."

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," Benton said. "It allows for that development very strategically, that considers compatibility and how it's integrated into both the county's need for infrastructure, need for quality of life, jobs, and also connectivity to our interstate and roadway system."

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the design incorporates open space and includes an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. Lewis said she worries the development will change the rural landscape. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do," Lewis said. "We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like." The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher shot and killed; family member arrested in connection with death
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce community is mourning the loss of Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Es.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce community is mourning the loss of Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children. His family released a statement about his death asking people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online discussing any other details, noting this is still an active investigation and a deeply painful circumstance that impacts so many people.

Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as more than just an educator. Coleman said Barnes was really a pillar of the community and noted she didn't grow up with a dad, and some of her friends didn't either, so they really looked at him as a father figure. Coleman said Barnes made an impact on them life-long, noting she is 37 years old now and he was her teacher in 7th grade. She said they kept communication that long, well before social media even came around. Coleman and others are calling for justice as the homicide investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Second decomposed body found near US Highway 1 in Sebastian this week
cards.teaser: A heavily decomposed body was discovered in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, the second body found in the same area this week.
cards.body: A heavily decomposed body was found in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, prompting a death investigation by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. A caller reported finding the body shortly after 4 p.m. The body was located on the east side of US 1, across the street from where the body of James Thompson was found Monday. Detectives and Crime Scene Unit personnel are processing the area and working to identify the deceased. Investigators are working to determine whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.

cards.headline: Dale Mincey identified as suspect in fatal Fort Pierce shooting of 66-year-old man
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified Dale Mincey as the suspect connected to a shooting that killed 66-year-old Andre Leonard Barnes in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
The fatal shooting happened Tuesday at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce, was taken to a local hospital, where he died.

The suspect in this homicide investigation has been identified as Dale A. Mincey, 41, of Fort Pierce, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. At this time, Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County Public Schools. The sheriff's office said the homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: Parents sue Vero Beach over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed and reburied without consent
cards.body:
Two Vero Beach parents have filed an amended lawsuit against the City of Vero Beach, alleging their infant son's remains were accidentally disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and then reinterred without their knowledge or consent. Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo's son, identified only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old and was buried at the city-operated cemetery on Aug. 15, 2007, where his parents believed he had remained undisturbed for nearly 18 years.

The parents allege that sometime between the burial in 2007 and April 2025, maintenance or irrigation work was taking place near the burial site when heavy equipment breached the grave. The lawsuit alleges A.C.'s casket, contents, and remains were damaged or destroyed. According to the complaint, someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket and reinter the child without notifying or obtaining consent from the parents. The lawsuit claims the parents were deprived of the opportunity to participate in laying their son to rest again and were never informed that the burial site had allegedly been disturbed.

The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment. The lawsuit also alleges the city failed to protect the burial site and failed to follow Florida laws and administrative rules governing cemetery maintenance, disinterment and the handling of human remains. The parents say they did not learn what allegedly happened until April 2025. The lawsuit does not explain how they became aware of the alleged disturbance, but an attorney for the family said that information could come out during the legal proceedings. The family's attorneys did not rule out the possibility of seeking to exhume the gravesite as part of the litigation.

This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false. Instead, the court ruled the legal claims, as originally pleaded, could not proceed against the city under Florida law. The City of Vero Beach declined to comment on the newly filed amended complaint. In court filings responding to the original lawsuit, the city disputed the parents' allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage. The city's attorney submitted a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C., with the closest sprinkler heads approximately 10 feet north and about 40 feet south of the burial plot. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint.

cards.headline: Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness holds fundraiser workout for family of 5-year-old killed in bike accident
cards.teaser: A Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness is rallying its community to support the family of 5-year-old Garrett Leonard, who was killed in an accident at a motocross park in Miami.
cards.body:
The gym is raising funds for the family of Garrett Leonard. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office says the 5-year-old was riding a bicycle in between vehicles at a motocross park in Miami and was hit when he crossed the path of a pick-up truck. MDSO says the driver cooperated in the investigation and told the gym on Wednesday that no charges had been filed in the case. His family was not ready to provide a statement Wednesday but shared photos.

Orangetheory coach Shelby Collier said she and gym owner Tabitha Lavery learned of the tragedy that struck two of their members and didn't hesitate to act. Collier said when she realized what happened it was heart wrenching and gut wrenching, and her first thought was that the community always comes together and they had to do this. Lavery described the couple as a great couple and valued members of the community. Collier reflected on the pride Garrett's father showed for his son, saying this is Garrett, look what he did, look what he did, and just the proudest dad. Lavery said they put together a fundraiser workout lasting 90 minutes to help the family get through this hard time. All of the proceeds will go toward a GoFundMe started to ease the financial burden that comes with losing a loved one. The workout is this Sunday and is open to the public.

hero.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of August debut
hero.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League announced the nicknames and logos for its four teams on Wednesday, with the inaugural season set to begin August 1 in Springfield, Illinois.
hero.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams on Wednesday ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Star pitcher Kelsie Whitmore, the first overall draft pick, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens alongside veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The league also includes the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

Each team name honors a groundbreaking woman from history. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. Their logo includes graphic lines surrounding a baseball, mimicking the speed of a fastball and resembling the New York skyline. The San Francisco Firebells honor Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who championed San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. Their logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The logo is a capital Q topped with four baseball diamonds. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist. Their logo is an osprey clasping a baseball bat in its talons.

The league's debut season begins on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois, where games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium. The season will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. The league has been years in the making and hopes to create a space for women's baseball players similar to the one the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League provided 70 years ago.

"This is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball," Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March, "and now for us to actually be with each other there's so much freedom and peace within it." With team identities now established, the Women's Professional Baseball League is set to launch its inaugural season and provide professional opportunities for women baseball players who have long awaited such a platform.

cards.headline: Messi scores eighth World Cup goal as Argentina rallies from two down to beat Egypt 3-2
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and Argentina completed a comeback from 2-0 down with 11 minutes remaining to defeat Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Argentina trailed Egypt 2-0 before scoring three goals in the final 11 minutes to win 3-2 on Tuesday in a World Cup round of 16 match. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute. Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 21st World Cup goal in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time. Messi was in tears after the final whistle. The goal was Messi's eighth of the tournament.

The defending champions will face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Argentina had trailed on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. Messi missed a penalty kick in the first half when Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir saved his shot. Messi later hit the post when the score was 1-0. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back World Cup titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. The 39-year-old Messi is playing in what might be the last of his six World Cups. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said he was emotional after the match.

cards.headline: United States loses 4-1 to Belgium in World Cup round of 16
cards.teaser: The United States was eliminated from the World Cup on Monday night when Belgium won 4-1 at Lumen Field in Seattle, ending American hopes for a deep run at the home tournament.
cards.body:
The United States' hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium to a 4-1 win Monday night that earned a quarterfinal berth. De Ketelaere put Belgium ahead in the eighth minute, the first time in this year's World Cup the U.S. conceded first. Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 midway through the first half with his second free kick goal of the tournament, energizing a largely red-white-and-blue crowd of 66,925 at Lumen Field. Belgium answered just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff when De Ketelaere headed the ball past goalkeeper Matt Freese in the 33rd minute. Freese's gaffe gave Belgium a third goal early in the second half when he chested a long ball, hesitated with a touch, then kicked the ball off De Ketelaere. Hans Vanaken one-timed a shot from 35 yards that deflected in off Tim Ream. Second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time after Belgium stripped the ball from Chris Richards.

American star Christian Pulisic injured his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt and was replaced seven minutes later. Belgium extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games and will play Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco. After winning three games in a World Cup for the first time in this expanded 48-nation tournament, the U.S. failed to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002. All six CONCACAF nations have been eliminated from the tournament. All quarterfinalists will come from Europe, South America and Africa.

cards.headline: United States-Belgium World Cup match draws record 30 million viewers on Fox
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match became the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history with more than 30 million viewers, Fox Sports reported.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, drawing more than 30 million viewers on Fox Sports, the network reported. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of the match, which the United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
cards.teaser: The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end the three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
cards.body:
The International Olympic Committee advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said. The move was expected since the IOC advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity.

Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem, saying that decision will come at an appropriate time. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal opening October 31. The IOC said Russian athletes must give multiple doping controls and be part of a recognized testing program to address the lack of confidence in the global sporting community relating to the return of Russian athletes to international competition.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach in November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, organizers with Under The Sun Promotions, Inc announced Monday.

The annual festival brings seafood vendors, local businesses, and entertainment to Vero Beach each year. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc is producing the event.

The festival has become a regular attraction for Treasure Coast residents and visitors looking for local seafood and family entertainment. Organizers announced the festival's return earlier this week.

Specific dates, venue location, and vendor information for the November event have been announced by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The festival has been held annually in Vero Beach for the past 17 years.

hero.headline: Former Florida gubernatorial candidate Andrew Gillum arrested on drug possession charges in Alabama
hero.teaser: The ex-Tallahassee mayor and 2018 Democratic candidate for governor was arrested on marijuana and methamphetamine possession charges after a traffic stop.
hero.body:
Former Florida gubernatorial candidate Andrew Gillum has been arrested on drug possession charges in Alabama after police say they pulled him over for erratic driving and found marijuana and meth in his vehicle. Gillum, 46, was arrested on July 2 in Daphne, about 11 miles east of Mobile on Alabama's Gulf Coast. He is charged with marijuana possession and unlawful possession of a controlled substance, the Daphne Police Department said. Jail records show he was released on July 3.

The Daphne Police Department said officers stopped Gillum's vehicle around 10:45 p.m. and initiated a probable cause search after one of them noticed a glass pipe on the center console. They found several rolled marijuana cigarettes and three packages of a substance that tested positive for methamphetamine, police said. Court records for Gillum's case were not yet available, according to the Baldwin County Clerk of Court's office. Information on a lawyer who could speak on his behalf was not immediately available.

Gillum served as mayor of Florida's capital from 2014 to 2018 and came within less than a percentage point of being elected the state's first Black governor, losing to Ron DeSantis by fewer than 34,000 votes. He was once considered a rising star of the Democratic Party. Gillum is a co-host of the politically themed Native Land Pod, which won the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding News and Information Podcast in 2025.

The arrest marks the latest legal trouble for Gillum. In 2020, he was found in a Miami Beach hotel room with a man who had apparently overdosed on drugs. Police said Gillum himself was too inebriated to talk about what happened. The man survived and no one was charged with a crime, but Gillum withdrew from public life for months afterward while seeking treatment for alcohol abuse and depression. In 2022, Gillum was indicted on federal conspiracy and wire fraud charges for allegedly funneling tens of thousands of dollars in campaign donations through third parties back to himself for personal use. A 2023 trial ended in a hung jury on those charges and an acquittal on charges that Gillum lied to undercover FBI agents posing as developers who paid for a 2016 trip he took with his brother to New York.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness hosts fundraiser workout for family of 5-year-old killed in bike accident
hero.body:
A Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness is hosting a fundraiser workout to support the family of Garrett Leonard, a 5-year-old boy killed in a bicycle accident. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office says Garrett was riding a bicycle between vehicles at a motocross park in Miami when he was hit after crossing the path of a pickup truck. The sheriff's office says the driver cooperated in the investigation and no charges had been filed as of Wednesday. The family was not ready to provide a statement Wednesday but shared photos with the news station.

Orangetheory coach Shelby Collier and gym owner Tabitha Lavery organized the fundraiser after learning two of their members had lost their son. Collier said the tragedy affected her deeply as both a coach and a parent. "When I realized what happened it was just heart wrenching, I mean gut wrenching," Collier said. "My first thought was like we always come together as a community here and I just thought, we have to do this." She added that as a parent she cannot even imagine that type of pain and believes the only thing that can get people through such circumstances is being supported.

Lavery described the couple as valued members of the community and said they are a great couple. Collier reflected on interactions she had witnessed with Garrett's father at the gym, recalling how he would proudly share his son's accomplishments. "This is Garrett, look what he did, look what he did, and just the proudest dad," Collier said. Lavery emphasized the importance of helping the family in any way possible during this difficult time. "We put together this fundraiser workout, it's 90 minutes, to help them get through this hard time," Lavery said.

The gym is hosting the 90-minute fundraiser workout this Sunday and it is open to the public. All proceeds from the event will go toward a GoFundMe that was started to ease the financial burden that comes with losing a loved one. The Orangetheory community is rallying together to provide support for the grieving family during an unimaginably difficult time.

hero.headline: 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95 moves forward despite neighbor opposition
hero.teaser: A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but neighbors say it will transform the area's rural character.
hero.body:
The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land off Indrio Road and Russakis Road near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August. The proposed development is 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres, equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches.

Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades. Lewis said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "I have dogs that have 10 acres to run around. I have horses that have 10 acres to run around. It's gone," Lewis said. She added that she thinks there are plenty of other places for them to build. Lewis also expressed concern about how the development will change the rural landscape in St. Lucie County. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do," said Lewis. "We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like."

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," said Benton. "It allows for that development very strategically, that considers compatibility and how it's integrated into both the county's need for infrastructure, need for quality of life, jobs, and also connectivity to our interstate and roadway system."

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Barnes killed in shooting; family member Dale Mincey arrested
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce community is mourning the loss of Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Es.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce community is mourning the loss of Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher killed in a shooting Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children. His family released a statement saying they are sad to report the loss of their dad to a senseless act of violence. The family asked people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online discussing any other details as this remains an active investigation.

Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as more than just an educator. Coleman said Barnes was really a pillar of the community and that she and friends who didn't grow up with dads looked at him as a father figure. Coleman, now 37 years old, said Barnes made an impact on students that was lifelong. She said they had kept communication well before social media even came around, which says a lot about his character. Coleman and others are calling for justice as the homicide investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at local pools this summer
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County residents and visitors will have the chance to learn life-saving skills this summer through free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors can attend free rip current safety demonstrations at local public pools this summer. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies and that the demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love.

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations. The first is July 19 from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. The second is July 28 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event with no registration required on a first-come, first-served basis. The third is August 16 from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. The hands-on training aims to build swimmer confidence and prepare participants for real ocean conditions before they head to area beaches.

cards.headline: Dale Mincey identified as suspect in fatal Fort Pierce shooting of 66-year-old man
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified Dale Mincey as the suspect connected to a shooting that killed 66-year-old Andre Leonard Barnes in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
The fatal shooting happened Tuesday at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce, was taken to a local hospital, where he died.

The suspect in this homicide investigation has been identified as Dale A. Mincey, 41, of Fort Pierce, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. At this time, Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County Public Schools. The sheriff's office said the homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public.

cards.teaser: Three free rip current safety demonstrations are scheduled at St. Lucie County public pools this summer using a new simulation machine.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents and visitors can attend free rip current safety demonstrations this summer at local public pools. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using a new rip current simulation machine that creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The proper technique when caught in a rip current is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

hero.headline: Parents sue Vero Beach over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed and reburied without consent
hero.body:
Two Vero Beach parents have filed an amended lawsuit against the City of Vero Beach, alleging their infant son's remains were accidentally disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and then reinterred without their knowledge or consent. Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo's son, identified only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old and was buried at the city-operated cemetery on Aug. 15, 2007, where his parents believed he had remained undisturbed for nearly 18 years.

The parents allege that sometime between the burial in 2007 and April 2025, maintenance or irrigation work was taking place near the burial site when heavy equipment breached the grave. The lawsuit alleges A.C.'s casket, contents, and remains were damaged or destroyed. According to the complaint, someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket and reinter the child without notifying or obtaining consent from the parents. The lawsuit claims the parents were deprived of the opportunity to participate in laying their son to rest again and were never informed that the burial site had allegedly been disturbed.

The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment. The lawsuit also alleges the city failed to protect the burial site and failed to follow Florida laws and administrative rules governing cemetery maintenance, disinterment and the handling of human remains. The parents say they did not learn what allegedly happened until April 2025. The lawsuit does not explain how they became aware of the alleged disturbance, but an attorney for the family said that information could come out during the legal proceedings. The family's attorneys did not rule out the possibility of seeking to exhume the gravesite as part of the litigation.

This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false. Instead, the court ruled the legal claims, as originally pleaded, could not proceed against the city under Florida law. The City of Vero Beach declined to comment on the newly filed amended complaint. In court filings responding to the original lawsuit, the city disputed the parents' allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage. The city's attorney submitted a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C., with the closest sprinkler heads approximately 10 feet north and about 40 feet south of the burial plot. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint.

cards.headline: Second decomposed body found near US Highway 1 in Sebastian this week
cards.teaser: A heavily decomposed body was discovered in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, the second body found in the same area this week.
cards.body: A heavily decomposed body was found in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, prompting a death investigation by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. A caller reported finding the body shortly after 4 p.m. The body was located on the east side of US 1, across the street from where the body of James Thompson was found Monday. Detectives and Crime Scene Unit personnel are processing the area and working to identify the deceased. Investigators are working to determine whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.
